---
title: Which package do I need?
description: The three NimbleBrain packages — nimblebrain-server-sdk, @nimblebrain/synapse and @nimblebrain/sdk — what each is for, and how an app pairs them with FastMCP.
---

Three packages, two registries. Which you need depends on what you are building.

| Package | Registry | Language | What it is for |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`nimblebrain-server-sdk`](https://pypi.org/project/nimblebrain-server-sdk/) | PyPI | Python | **The server.** Tool annotations, change announcements, the `ai.nimblebrain` extensions, skills and the error contract, with database access, observability and notifications as extras. [Docs](/server-sdk/quickstart/) |
| [`@nimblebrain/synapse`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nimblebrain/synapse) | npm | TypeScript | **An app's interface.** The part that runs in the browser: calling tools, staying in sync with the agent, theming. [Docs](https://synapse.nimblebrain.ai/docs/quickstart-react/) |
| [`@nimblebrain/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nimblebrain/sdk) | npm | TypeScript | **The API client.** A program that calls NimbleBrain's API from outside. Not used to build a server. |

Serving the interface from the server needs no NimbleBrain package. It is the MCP Apps standard, which FastMCP 4 implements in `fastmcp.apps`.

## By what you are building

| You are building | Install |
|---|---|
| A connector: a server alone | `nimblebrain-server-sdk` |
| An app: a server plus its interface | `nimblebrain-server-sdk` in the server, which serves the interface with FastMCP's `AppConfig`; `@nimblebrain/synapse` in the interface |
| A program that calls NimbleBrain | `@nimblebrain/sdk` |
| A server in another language | None. Implement the protocol from the "Wire (any SDK)" tabs, starting at [MCP extensions](/extensions/overview/) |

## How an app fits together

The interface is built with `@nimblebrain/synapse` to one self-contained HTML file. The server is a FastMCP 4 server with the Server SDK. It serves that file as a `ui://` resource and binds tools to it, both with `fastmcp.apps.AppConfig`:

```python
from fastmcp.apps import AppConfig, ResourceCSP

@mcp.resource("ui://tasks/main", app=AppConfig(prefers_border=True, csp=ResourceCSP()))
def tasks_ui() -> str:
    return UI_HTML

@mcp.tool(app=AppConfig(resource_uri="ui://tasks/main", visibility=["model", "app"]))
async def list_tasks() -> dict: ...
```

| | Version |
|---|---|
| `nimblebrain-server-sdk` | 0.7 or later |
| FastMCP | 4.0 or later |
| Python | 3.13 or later |

Synapse's [Serve a Synapse UI from a FastMCP server](https://synapse.nimblebrain.ai/docs/quickstart-python/) walks through it, and [ChatGPT compatibility](https://synapse.nimblebrain.ai/docs/guides/chatgpt/) covers the keys only ChatGPT reads. NimbleBrain's own additions for a view (placements, theming, the bridge) are under [App Views](/apps/overview/).

The two packages do different jobs and do not overlap: the Server SDK is what the server shares with NimbleBrain's host, and Synapse is what the interface uses to reach the server, on any host.
